knowledge:
- key_parameters: groupNames=A character vector defining the common prefix parts of the single-stained control names (e.g., Beads, Dead) used to group controls in specMatCalc ;; autoFluoName=The file name of the unstained control in specMatCalc used for autofluorescence correction ;; transNames=A character vector of channel names to be transformed in arcTrans ;; saveResult=A logical parameter in oneVsAllPlot indicating whether to save the generated plots to a folder (defaults to TRUE) ;; idInfo=A list of regular expressions in flowSet2LongDf used to parse and extract metadata from FCS file names into separate dataframe columns.
- alternatives: flowVS is mentioned as an alternative automated strategy for cofactor estimation and transformation, which can make the manual cofactor selection in arcTrans unnecessary.
- when_to_use: Use this package when you have raw spectral cytometry data (such as Cytek Aurora FCS files) and single-stained controls, and you need to perform spectral unmixing, transform the data, inspect and manually correct unmixing artifacts, and export the clean data to a tidy dataframe format.
- pitfalls: Setting global cofactors in arcTrans without individual adjustment can create artifactual populations if there is too much resolution around zero. Unmixing artifacts (such as false negative correlations) are common and must be corrected using a secondary symmetric correction matrix (corrMatCreate and correctUnmix) to prevent downstream clustering errors. Over-correction can lead to undermixing/bleed-over, so correction values must be carefully calibrated (e.g., starting with small negative values like -0.03).

workflows.name: spectral_cytometry_preprocessing
workflows.intent: Perform spectral unmixing, arcsinh transformation, artifact correction, and export spectral cytometry data to a long dataframe.
input: unmixCtrls (flowSet of single-stained control FCS files)
fullPanel (flowFrame of the fully stained sample FCS file)
workflows.stages: 1. Calculate the spectral unmixing matrix using single-stained controls with specMatCalc ;; 2. Perform spectral unmixing on the fully stained sample with specUnmix ;; 3. Transform the unmixed data using arcsinh transformation with arcTrans ;; 4. Visualize potential unmixing artifacts with oneVsAllPlot ;; 5. Create a correction matrix with corrMatCreate ;; 6. Correct unmixing artifacts with correctUnmix ;; 7. Convert the processed flowSet to a long dataframe with extracted metadata using flowSet2LongDf
workflows.code:
specMat <- specMatCalc(unmixCtrls, groupNames = c("Beads_", "Dead_"), autoFluoName = "PBMC_unstained.fcs")
fullPanelUnmix <- specUnmix(fullPanel, specMat)
fullPanelTrans <- arcTrans(fullPanelUnmix, transNames = colnames(fullPanelUnmix)[6:18])
oneVsAllPlot(fullPanelTrans, "AF647_IgM", saveResult = FALSE)
corrMat <- corrMatCreate(specMat)
corrMat["BV650_CD56", "AF647_IgM"] <- -0.03
fullPanelCorr <- correctUnmix(fullPanelUnmix, corrMat)
oneVsAllPlot(fullPanelCorr, "AF647_IgM", saveResult = FALSE)
fullPanelFs <- flowSet(fullPanelTrans)
sampleNames(fullPanelFs) <- "PBMC_full_panel_d1.fcs"
fullPanelDf <- flowSet2LongDf(fullPanelFs, idInfo = list("Tissue" = "|_full_panel_..\\.fcs", "Donor" = "...._full_panel_|\\.fcs"))
